title: Analysis of local protein accumulation kinetics by live-cell imaging in yeast systems
protocol: Streak out the strain(s) of interest on YPD plates.
Incubate the streaked strains for 1–2 days at 25°C or 30°C.
Inoculate cells from a single colony into 4 mL of SC liquid medium in a test tube.
Shake the inoculated medium at 25°C for 6–8 hours in a water bath shaker (at 210 rpm).
For fission yeast, inoculate cells from a single colony into 8 mL of YE5S liquid medium in a test tube.
Shake the inoculated medium at 25°C for 6–8 hours in a water bath shaker (at 210 rpm).
Transfer preculture to 4 mL of SC medium in a test tube and shake them at 25°C overnight for 12–16 hours in a water bath shaker (at 210 rpm).
Concentrate cells by centrifugation and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet to 150 μL fresh SC medium.
Transfer 1 mL of mid-log culture to a low retention microcentrifuge tube for harvesting cells.
Declump cells by sonication for 5 seconds at 15% power if they form aggregates.
Centrifuge concentrated cells at 8,000 × g and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in fresh SC medium.
Place the entire cell suspension into the Con A/Lectin-coated glass-bottom dish.
Mount the dish on the microscope stage and incubate for 5–15 minutes to allow cells to sediment.
Check the cell density on the glass bottom by microscopy during sedimentation.
Remove the supernatant when an appropriate cell density is reached (50-70% field coverage).
Wash the cells with 200 μL of fresh SC medium, repeating 2–3 times to remove floating and unattached cells.
Gently aspirate the supernatant after washing.
Add 1-1.5 mL of SC medium to the dish.
Note: Use YE5S medium for fission yeast.
Leave a small amount of supernatant when changing media to prevent cell drying.
Critical: Avoid overcrowded fields (90-100% field coverage).
